news.title: European Central Bank raises interest rates a quarter point to quell energy-fueled inflation
news.summary: The European Central Bank raised interest rates Thursday to cool inflation that is being fed by high oil prices from the Iran war.  The central bank for the 21 EU member countries that use the euro currency raised its benchmark rate by a quarter percentage point to 2.50% at a meeting held in Berlin, away from the bank’s Frankfurt headquarters.  The bank said in an accompanying statement that “the conflict in the Middle East continues to generate inflation pressures, and inflation is set to remain well above target for an extended period.”
